chunk_findings.detail: `FakeDigest.content_digest` caps the generated hex chain at `WIDTH = 64` before applying `size`. If `size` is the digest size in bytes, as `of_obj`’s default `size=12` (24 hex chars) implies, then `FakeDigest().content_digest(b"x", algo="blake2b", size=64)` returns a 64-character hex string instead of the 128 characters requested by `size * 2`; the same happens for `of_obj({}, size=64)`. A port/conformance case that requests a valid 64-byte blake2b-style digest gets a silently truncated 32-byte fake, so the fake does not pass the same cases as the real adapter.

chunk_findings.detail: `Fsio.file_lock` (and `temp_text` at line 35) are documented as context-manager contracts (“released on exit”, “removed on exit”), but their return annotations are `Iterator[...]`. A caller using the documented pattern `with fsio.file_lock(path):` is using a value typed as `Iterator[Any]`, which is not a context manager and has no `__enter__`/`__exit__`; conversely, an implementation that literally returns an `Iterator` is a plain generator, so entering it with `with` raises `AttributeError`. A typical correct implementation using `contextlib.contextmanager` returns `ContextManager[...]`, which does not satisfy the declared `Iterator[...]` contract.

chunk_findings.detail: `port` marks a Protocol by setting a non-callable class attribute `__ddflow_port__ = True`. The old ports were `@runtime_checkable`, and any new family module that keeps that decorator in order to preserve structural checks will now have a runtime-checkable Protocol with a non-method member. For example, after `@port @runtime_checkable class HttpClient(Protocol): def request(...): ...`, a call such as `issubclass(FakeHttpClient, HttpClient)` raises `TypeError: Protocols with non-method members don't support issubclass()` even when the fake implements `request`; before this marker existed, that check could return True. This is a behaviour change and breaks conformance/caller structural checks that rely on runtime protocols [D-adapters-answers]. The marker should be kept outside the Protocol class (for example, in a global set or external registry) rather than as a class attribute.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_literal` shortcut treats every all-caps `ast.Name` as harmless. That helper is used by the declaration-only check, whose docstring explicitly says nothing may run “in a body, a decorator or a base.” Given a port module with `ALL_CAPS = some_decorator` and a class written as `@port` / `@ALL_CAPS` / `class P(Protocol): ...`, the decorator expression is an all-caps `Name`, so `_literal` returns `True` and the test accepts the class even though class creation calls `ALL_CAPS` and can run arbitrary code. chunk_findings.detail: The new file-based baseline is only checked one way: every port without a fake must have a baseline file, and baseline files may not name a port that already has a fake. chunk_findings.detail: The conformance test is supposed to run the cases against the fake registered in `F.FAKES`, but it constructs the fake as `entry.get("fake", F.FAKES[name])()`. chunk_findings.detail: `FakeDigest.content_digest` fills `out` only to `self.WIDTH` (64 hex characters) before slicing it by `size * 2`. chunk_findings.detail: `port` adds an arbitrary non-callable class attribute `__ddflow_port__ = True` to every Protocol it marks. The removed definitions in this same file show all moved ports (`Proc`, `Git`, `Fsio`, `Toml`, `Digest`, `HttpClient`) were `@runtime_checkable`; to keep being discovered they must now also be decorated with `@port`. But `typing.Protocol` treats any non-callable member (other than its whitelisted dunders) as a non-method member, and `runtime_checkable` Protocols with non-method members do not support `isinstance`. For example, if a moved port is `@port`-marked and still `@runtime_checkable`, then `isinstance(some_object, ThatPort)` raises `TypeError` instead of returning True/False, breaking the existing runtime port checks that the old file explicitly enabled.

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeDigest` treats `size` only as a post-hoc truncation of a fixed CRC chain and caps that chain at `WIDTH = 64` hex characters. As a result, a requested `size` larger than 32 bytes is silently shortened: `FakeDigest().of_obj({}, size=64)` returns a 64-character hex string instead of the 128 characters implied by a 64-byte digest (and `content_digest(..., size=33)` returns 64 characters instead of 66). Worse, because `size` does not change the underlying chain, different `size` inputs can collapse to the same output when `length` is fixed: `FakeDigest().of_obj({}, size=12, length=24)` and `FakeDigest().of_obj({}, size=13, length=24)` both return the same first 24 hex characters, violating the fake’s stated “different inputs differ” property and any conformance case that treats `size` as a distinct digest-size input.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/digest.py:36

chunk_findings.detail: These methods are documented as context managers (“released on exit”, “removed on exit”) but are annotated as returning plain `Iterator` objects. A fake or adapter that satisfies the annotation by returning a generator, e.g. `def file_lock(self, path, *, timeout=None): yield`, is not a context manager, so the documented usage `with fsio.file_lock(path): ...` raises `AttributeError`/`TypeError` because the generator lacks `__enter__`/`__exit__`. Conversely, an implementation that correctly uses `@contextmanager` returns a `ContextManager`, not an `Iterator`, so it violates the protocol’s return annotation under structural type checking. The contract should require a context-manager type such as `ContextManager[Any]` and `ContextManager[Path]`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fsio.py: `Fsio.file_lock`, `Fsio.temp_text`

chunk_findings.detail: `port` is annotated as `(cls: Any) -> Any`, so using it as a class decorator erases the protocol type for static checkers. For example, after `@port class HttpClient(Protocol): ...`, an annotation such as `def send(client: HttpClient): ...` is typed `Any` by mypy, so passing an object without `request` is not reported. This defeats the stated purpose of ports being structural `Protocol` types and changes the static behaviour from the old `ports.py`, where `HttpClient` was a `Protocol`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/ports.py:port

chunk_findings.detail: `discover` keys the result by `cls.__name__` and silently overwrites duplicates. If `ddflow/adapters/alpha.py` and `ddflow/adapters/beta.py` both define `@port class Cache(Protocol): ...`, `discover(ddflow.adapters)` returns only the `Cache` from the later module (`beta`), not the one from `alpha`. The generic conformance test then sees only one `Cache` port, so a missing fake or missing baseline line for `alpha.Cache` would not fail the test. Duplicate port names should either be namespaced by module or rejected loudly, not dropped silently.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/ports.py:discover

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion intended to pin deterministic sorted-module discovery is self-referential: the expected list is built by iterating `found` itself, so it only checks that discovery order agrees with `P.module_names(A)`, not that `P.module_names(A)` is sorted. If the filesystem/environment causes `P.module_names(A)` to return `['zoo', 'alpha']` and `P.discover(A)` iterates that same order, `found` is `['ZooPort', 'AlphaPort']` and the RHS is also `['ZooPort', 'AlphaPort']`, so the test passes even though ports are not in sorted module order, contrary to the stated “sorted module names, no hash order” requirement.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ports_contract.py:test_the_ports_are_found_by_scanning_not_listed

chunk_findings.detail: The refactor no longer checks that `ddflow/adapters/ports.py` itself is declaration-only. `test_a_port_is_a_declaration_only` parses each discovered port module but filters the AST to classes with a `@port` decorator, and the only replacement for the old module-wide `test_ports_are_declarations_only` is `test_the_ports_base_imports_the_standard_library_alone`, which inspects imports. Therefore, if `ddflow/adapters/ports.py` is edited to add any executable non-`@port` code, e.g. `class Helper: print("imported")`, both new tests pass while the shared ports base now runs code at import time. The old test would have failed, so the change no longer enforces the stated invariant that `ports.py` is a pure base.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ports_contract.py:test_a_port_is_a_declaration_only

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert list(found) == expect and sorted(F.FAKES) == sorted(found)` only compares the *keys* of the global fake registry with the keys returned by `F.collect(F)`. It never checks that the values in `F.FAKES` are the fake classes discovered by `F.collect(F)`, nor that `F.FAKES` itself is in sorted module order. For example, if a previous test or a bad registration leaves `F.FAKES['Digest'] = object()` while `F.collect(F)` returns `{'Digest': FakeDigest}` and the expected sorted module grouping, both `list(found) == expect` and `sorted(F.FAKES) == sorted(found)` are true, so this test passes even though the actual registry used by `test_adapter_and_fake_pass_the_same_cases` contains the wrong fake. The test should compare values/identity (or compare `F.FAKES` directly to the discovered registry) rather than only sorted key sets.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ports_contract.py:test_fakes_register_in_sorted_module_order

chunk_findings.detail: The old module exposed `FakeDigest` as a top-level class and `FakeHttpClient` via `from .http import FakeHttpClient`, so `from ddflow.adapters.fakes import FakeDigest` or `from ddflow.adapters.fakes import FakeHttpClient` worked. The new code only runs `collect(...)`, and `importlib.import_module` of each submodule sets the submodule attributes `fakes.digest` and `fakes.http`, not the contained class attributes. Thus `ddflow.adapters.fakes.FakeDigest` now raises `AttributeError` and the old direct imports raise `ImportError`. This is a behavior change for shipped fakes and violates the no-behaviour-change requirement [D-adapters-answers].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/__init__.py:package namespace

chunk_findings.detail: The per-family docs for forge, fsio, git, proc and tomlcfg still say the default adapter is `ddflow.infra.<family>` (“Default adapter: `ddflow.infra.forge` today”). Under this change, `ddflow/adapters/<family>.py` is the family module that owns the port, default adapter and registry entry, so these docs point readers to the old pre-change location. A reader following `docs/ddflow/adapters/forge.md` is told to use `ddflow.infra.forge` rather than the new canonical `ddflow.adapters.forge` (same issue in `fsio.md:7`, `git.md:7`, `proc.md:7`, `tomlcfg.md:7`).

chunk_findings.detail: The `HttpClient` conformance entry sets `"real": ScriptedUrllib`. But `ScriptedUrllib` is the scripted replacement for urllib calls used by the default adapter to avoid the network, not an implementation of the `HttpClient` port. The port interface is exercised by `http_conformance` as a `request` API, while `ScriptedUrllib` provides the transport/urllib side. When `pytest tests/test_ports_contract.py` runs the discovered http family via this `CONFORMANCE`, it will call `http_conformance` against `ScriptedUrllib` instead of the real `HttpClient` wired to `ScriptedUrllib`, and the cases will fail with an `AttributeError`/`TypeError` because the object does not implement the adapter's `request` method.

chunk_findings.detail: The `expr.id.isupper()` branch makes any all-caps `ast.Name` count as a literal. `_literal` is used by `_opaque`/`_class_code` to detect runtime code in a `@port` class, so this lets executable name references pass. The test's own wording says `frozenset(...)` is code “however cheap”, and a `LOAD_NAME` for `TIMEOUT` is runtime code too; this false negative weakens the declaration-only invariant the test is meant to enforce.

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeDigest.content_digest` caps the generated hex chain at `WIDTH = 64` before applying `size`. If `size` is the digest size in bytes, as `of_obj`’s default `size=12` (24 hex chars) implies, then `FakeDigest().content_digest(b"x", algo="blake2b", size=64)` returns a 64-character hex string instead of the 128 characters requested by `size * 2`; the same happens for `of_obj({}, size=64)`. A port/conformance case that requests a valid 64-byte blake2b-style digest gets a silently truncated 32-byte fake, so the fake does not pass the same cases as the real adapter.

chunk_findings.detail: `Fsio.file_lock` (and `temp_text` at line 35) are documented as context-manager contracts (“released on exit”, “removed on exit”), but their return annotations are `Iterator[...]`. A caller using the documented pattern `with fsio.file_lock(path):` is using a value typed as `Iterator[Any]`, which is not a context manager and has no `__enter__`/`__exit__`; conversely, an implementation that literally returns an `Iterator` is a plain generator, so entering it with `with` raises `AttributeError`. A typical correct implementation using `contextlib.contextmanager` returns `ContextManager[...]`, which does not satisfy the declared `Iterator[...]` contract.

chunk_findings.detail: `port` marks a Protocol by setting a non-callable class attribute `__ddflow_port__ = True`. The old ports were `@runtime_checkable`, and any new family module that keeps that decorator in order to preserve structural checks will now have a runtime-checkable Protocol with a non-method member. For example, after `@port @runtime_checkable class HttpClient(Protocol): def request(...): ...`, a call such as `issubclass(FakeHttpClient, HttpClient)` raises `TypeError: Protocols with non-method members don't support issubclass()` even when the fake implements `request`; before this marker existed, that check could return True. This is a behaviour change and breaks conformance/caller structural checks that rely on runtime protocols [D-adapters-answers]. The marker should be kept outside the Protocol class (for example, in a global set or external registry) rather than as a class attribute.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `_literal` shortcut treats every all-caps `ast.Name` as harmless. That helper is used by the declaration-only check, whose docstring explicitly says nothing may run “in a body, a decorator or a base.” Given a port module with `ALL_CAPS = some_decorator` and a class written as `@port` / `@ALL_CAPS` / `class P(Protocol): ...`, the decorator expression is an all-caps `Name`, so `_literal` returns `True` and the test accepts the class even though class creation calls `ALL_CAPS` and can run arbitrary code. The same shortcut also lets a method body consisting of a bare all-caps name pass, which is neither a docstring nor `...` and is not a literal.

chunk_findings.detail: The new file-based baseline is only checked one way: every port without a fake must have a baseline file, and baseline files may not name a port that already has a fake. It never checks that a baseline file names a declared port at all. If the `Git` port is removed (or `discover()` fails to find it) but `tests/ports_without_fake/Git.txt` is left behind, `_without_fake()` returns `{"Git"}`, `Git` is in `_CEILING`, `missing` does not contain it, and `baseline & have` is empty, so the test passes even though the baseline file is no longer for a missing port. If a `Git` port is later added without a fake, the stale baseline file excuses it, violating the stated invariant that a new port cannot be excused.

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeDigest.content_digest` fills `out` only to `self.WIDTH` (64 hex characters) before slicing it by `size * 2`. For `size` values above 32, the result is silently shorter than the requested number of bytes: for example `FakeDigest().content_digest(b"x", "blake2b", size=48)` returns 64 hex characters, not the 96 hex characters a `blake2b` digest of `digest_size=48` must produce. chunk_findings.detail: `port` adds an arbitrary non-callable class attribute `__ddflow_port__ = True` to every Protocol it marks. The removed definitions in this same file show all moved ports (`Proc`, `Git`, `Fsio`, `Toml`, `Digest`, `HttpClient`) were `@runtime_checkable`; to keep being discovered they must now also be decorated with `@port`. But `typing.Protocol` treats any non-callable member (other than its whitelisted dunders) as a non-method member, and `runtime_checkable` Protocols with non-method members do not support `isinstance`. For example, if a moved port is `@port`-marked and still `@runtime_checkable`, then `isinstance(some_object, ThatPort)` raises `TypeError` instead of returning True/False, breaking the existing runtime port checks that the old file explicitly enabled.

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeDigest` treats `size` only as a post-hoc truncation of a fixed CRC chain and caps that chain at `WIDTH = 64` hex characters. As a result, a requested `size` larger than 32 bytes is silently shortened: `FakeDigest().of_obj({}, size=64)` returns a 64-character hex string instead of the 128 characters implied by a 64-byte digest (and `content_digest(..., size=33)` returns 64 characters instead of 66). Worse, because `size` does not change the underlying chain, different `size` inputs can collapse to the same output when `length` is fixed: `FakeDigest().of_obj({}, size=12, length=24)` and `FakeDigest().of_obj({}, size=13, length=24)` both return the same first 24 hex characters, violating the fake’s stated “different inputs differ” property and any conformance case that treats `size` as a distinct digest-size input.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/digest.py:36

chunk_findings.detail: These methods are documented as context managers (“released on exit”, “removed on exit”) but are annotated as returning plain `Iterator` objects. A fake or adapter that satisfies the annotation by returning a generator, e.g. `def file_lock(self, path, *, timeout=None): yield`, is not a context manager, so the documented usage `with fsio.file_lock(path): ...` raises `AttributeError`/`TypeError` because the generator lacks `__enter__`/`__exit__`. Conversely, an implementation that correctly uses `@contextmanager` returns a `ContextManager`, not an `Iterator`, so it violates the protocol’s return annotation under structural type checking. The contract should require a context-manager type such as `ContextManager[Any]` and `ContextManager[Path]`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fsio.py: `Fsio.file_lock`, `Fsio.temp_text`

chunk_findings.detail: `port` is annotated as `(cls: Any) -> Any`, so using it as a class decorator erases the protocol type for static checkers. For example, after `@port class HttpClient(Protocol): ...`, an annotation such as `def send(client: HttpClient): ...` is typed `Any` by mypy, so passing an object without `request` is not reported. This defeats the stated purpose of ports being structural `Protocol` types and changes the static behaviour from the old `ports.py`, where `HttpClient` was a `Protocol`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/ports.py:port

chunk_findings.detail: `discover` keys the result by `cls.__name__` and silently overwrites duplicates. If `ddflow/adapters/alpha.py` and `ddflow/adapters/beta.py` both define `@port class Cache(Protocol): ...`, `discover(ddflow.adapters)` returns only the `Cache` from the later module (`beta`), not the one from `alpha`. The generic conformance test then sees only one `Cache` port, so a missing fake or missing baseline line for `alpha.Cache` would not fail the test. Duplicate port names should either be namespaced by module or rejected loudly, not dropped silently.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/ports.py:discover

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion intended to pin deterministic sorted-module discovery is self-referential: the expected list is built by iterating `found` itself, so it only checks that discovery order agrees with `P.module_names(A)`, not that `P.module_names(A)` is sorted. If the filesystem/environment causes `P.module_names(A)` to return `['zoo', 'alpha']` and `P.discover(A)` iterates that same order, `found` is `['ZooPort', 'AlphaPort']` and the RHS is also `['ZooPort', 'AlphaPort']`, so the test passes even though ports are not in sorted module order, contrary to the stated “sorted module names, no hash order” requirement.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ports_contract.py:test_the_ports_are_found_by_scanning_not_listed

chunk_findings.detail: The refactor no longer checks that `ddflow/adapters/ports.py` itself is declaration-only. `test_a_port_is_a_declaration_only` parses each discovered port module but filters the AST to classes with a `@port` decorator, and the only replacement for the old module-wide `test_ports_are_declarations_only` is `test_the_ports_base_imports_the_standard_library_alone`, which inspects imports. Therefore, if `ddflow/adapters/ports.py` is edited to add any executable non-`@port` code, e.g. `class Helper: print("imported")`, both new tests pass while the shared ports base now runs code at import time. The old test would have failed, so the change no longer enforces the stated invariant that `ports.py` is a pure base.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ports_contract.py:test_a_port_is_a_declaration_only

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert list(found) == expect and sorted(F.FAKES) == sorted(found)` only compares the *keys* of the global fake registry with the keys returned by `F.collect(F)`. It never checks that the values in `F.FAKES` are the fake classes discovered by `F.collect(F)`, nor that `F.FAKES` itself is in sorted module order. For example, if a previous test or a bad registration leaves `F.FAKES['Digest'] = object()` while `F.collect(F)` returns `{'Digest': FakeDigest}` and the expected sorted module grouping, both `list(found) == expect` and `sorted(F.FAKES) == sorted(found)` are true, so this test passes even though the actual registry used by `test_adapter_and_fake_pass_the_same_cases` contains the wrong fake. The test should compare values/identity (or compare `F.FAKES` directly to the discovered registry) rather than only sorted key sets.

chunk_findings.detail: The old module exposed `FakeDigest` as a top-level class and `FakeHttpClient` via `from .http import FakeHttpClient`, so `from ddflow.adapters.fakes import FakeDigest` or `from ddflow.adapters.fakes import FakeHttpClient` worked. The new code only runs `collect(...)`, and `importlib.import_module` of each submodule sets the submodule attributes `fakes.digest` and `fakes.http`, not the contained class attributes. Thus `ddflow.adapters.fakes.FakeDigest` now raises `AttributeError` and the old direct imports raise `ImportError`. This is a behavior change for shipped fakes and violates the no-behaviour-change requirement [D-adapters-answers].

chunk_findings.detail: The `HttpClient` conformance entry sets `"real": ScriptedUrllib`. But `ScriptedUrllib` is the scripted replacement for urllib calls used by the default adapter to avoid the network, not an implementation of the `HttpClient` port. The port interface is exercised by `http_conformance` as a `request` API, while `ScriptedUrllib` provides the transport/urllib side. When `pytest tests/test_ports_contract.py` runs the discovered http family via this `CONFORMANCE`, it will call `http_conformance` against `ScriptedUrllib` instead of the real `HttpClient` wired to `ScriptedUrllib`, and the cases will fail with an `AttributeError`/`TypeError` because the object does not implement the adapter's `request` method.

chunk_findings.detail: The `expr.id.isupper()` branch makes any all-caps `ast.Name` count as a literal. `_literal` is used by `_opaque`/`_class_code` to detect runtime code in a `@port` class, so this lets executable name references pass. For example, in `ddflow/adapters/http.py` define `TIMEOUT = 5` and then in the `@port` class use `def request(self, timeout: int = TIMEOUT) -> None: ...`; the default is evaluated at class-definition time, but `_literal(ast.Name("TIMEOUT"))` now returns `True`, so `_class_code` sees no statement and the test passes. Previously only `None`, `True`, and `False` names were allowed. The test's own wording says `frozenset(...)` is code “however cheap”, and a `LOAD_NAME` for `TIMEOUT` is runtime code too; this false negative weakens the declaration-only invariant the test is meant to enforce.

chunk_findings.detail: `expect` is derived from `found.items()`, so any fakes that discovery failed to register are omitted from both sides of the assertion. Given an environment where `F.collect` returns `{}` (e.g. the fake submodules are not imported, or the `fake` decorator no longer registers them), `expect` is also `[]`, so `list(found) == expect` is true and the test passes. The removed previous assertion compared `F.FAKES` against the explicit, non-empty `CASES`; with the new loops over `F.FAKES` also iterating zero entries when it is empty, broken fake discovery can leave all fake conformance checks silently unrun.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `size` fix ignores `length` when choosing how much of the CRC chain to generate. `want` is derived from `size * 2`, but the loop runs until `max(want, self.WIDTH)` even if the caller immediately truncates the result to a small `length`. For example, `FakeDigest().of_obj({"a": 1}, size=10**8, length=1)` should return one character quickly, but this code loops about 25 million times and builds a roughly 200 MB string before finally returning `out[:1]`. This is a new resource-exhaustion path introduced by the size fix; the loop only needs to generate up to `min(length, want)` when `length` is provided (or `want` when it is not).

chunk_findings.detail: The test’s name promises sorted-module registration, but the new assertions still do not pin sortedness of the module scan or of the global `FAKES` registry. `expect` is built by iterating `mods`, so if `P.module_names(F, frozenset())` returns `['zoo', 'alpha']` and `F.collect(F)`/`F.FAKES` are populated in that same order, then `list(found) == expect`, `all(F.FAKES[n] is c ...)`, `sorted(F.FAKES) == sorted(found)`, the module-set check, and the package-attribute check all pass even though the registry is not in sorted module order. Likewise, if `found` is sorted but `F.FAKES` insertion order is reversed, `sorted(F.FAKES) == sorted(found)` still passes because it compares only key sets. Thus an unsorted or nondeterministic fake registry can satisfy the test, contrary to the intended sorted-module discovery guarantee.

chunk_findings.detail: The new duplicate guard keys on `cls.__name__` but ignores the iteration variable `name`, so an alias to a decorated port class in the same module is misread as a second port. For example, if `ddflow/adapters/http.py` has `@port class HttpClient(Protocol): ...` followed by `PortAlias = HttpClient`, then `vars(module).items()` yields both names for the same class. Both entries pass `isinstance(cls, type) and cls.__dict__.get(MARK) and cls.__module__ == module.__name__`, and the alias then trips `if cls.__name__ in found`, raising `ValueError` even though there is only one port.

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeDigest.content_digest` caps the generated hex chain at `WIDTH = 64` before applying `size`. If `size` is the digest size in bytes, as `of_obj`’s default `size=12` (24 hex chars) implies, then `FakeDigest().content_digest(b"x", algo="blake2b", size=64)` returns a 64-character hex string instead of the 128 characters requested by `size * 2`; the same happens for `of_obj({}, size=64)`. A port/conformance case that requests a valid 64-byte blake2b-style digest gets a silently truncated 32-byte fake, so the fake does not pass the same cases as the real adapter.

chunk_findings.detail: `Fsio.file_lock` (and `temp_text` at line 35) are documented as context-manager contracts (“released on exit”, “removed on exit”), but their return annotations are `Iterator[...]`. A caller using the documented pattern `with fsio.file_lock(path):` is using a value typed as `Iterator[Any]`, which is not a context manager and has no `__enter__`/`__exit__`; conversely, an implementation that literally returns an `Iterator` is a plain generator, so entering it with `with` raises `AttributeError`. A typical correct implementation using `contextlib.contextmanager` returns `ContextManager[...]`, which does not satisfy the declared `Iterator[...]` contract.

chunk_findings.detail: The module docstring explicitly claims `Pure standard library; imports no other ddflow layer`, but this diff adds `from .ports import port`, which imports another `ddflow` module. This makes the stated import contract false: any import-graph guard or user relying on `ddflow.adapters.mcp` being standalone/stdlib-only (as documented) will now see a ddflow dependency when importing the module.

chunk_findings.detail: `port` marks a Protocol by setting a non-callable class attribute `__ddflow_port__ = True`. The old ports were `@runtime_checkable`, and any new family module that keeps that decorator in order to preserve structural checks will now have a runtime-checkable Protocol with a non-method member. For example, after `@port @runtime_checkable class HttpClient(Protocol): def request(...): ...`, a call such as `issubclass(FakeHttpClient, HttpClient)` raises `TypeError: Protocols with non-method members don't support issubclass()` even when the fake implements `request`; before this marker existed, that check could return True. This is a behaviour change and breaks conformance/caller structural checks that rely on runtime protocols [D-adapters-answers]. The marker should be kept outside the Protocol class (for example, in a global set or external registry) rather than as a class attribute.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/ports.py:port

chunk_findings.detail: The digest page states that the default adapter is `ddflow.core.digest` “today”, while `docs/ddflow/adapters/README.md` states that the default adapter is the ONE implementation in the family module `ddflow/adapters/<family>.py` and that `adapters` is the bottom layer importing no other ddflow layer. chunk_findings.detail: The new `_literal` shortcut treats every all-caps `ast.Name` as harmless. That helper is used by the declaration-only check, whose docstring explicitly says nothing may run “in a body, a decorator or a base.” Given a port module with `ALL_CAPS = some_decorator` and a class written as `@port` / `@ALL_CAPS` / `class P(Protocol): ...`, the decorator expression is an all-caps `Name`, so `_literal` returns `True` and the test accepts the class even though class creation calls `ALL_CAPS` and can run arbitrary code. The same shortcut also lets a method body consisting of a bare all-caps name pass, which is neither a docstring nor `...` and is not a literal.

chunk_findings.detail: The new file-based baseline is only checked one way: every port without a fake must have a baseline file, and baseline files may not name a port that already has a fake. It never checks that a baseline file names a declared port at all. If the `Git` port is removed (or `discover()` fails to find it) but `tests/ports_without_fake/Git.txt` is left behind, `_without_fake()` returns `{"Git"}`, `Git` is in `_CEILING`, `missing` does not contain it, and `baseline & have` is empty, so the test passes even though the baseline file is no longer for a missing port. chunk_findings.detail: `FakeDigest.content_digest` fills `out` only to `self.WIDTH` (64 hex characters) before slicing it by `size * 2`. For `size` values above 32, the result is silently shorter than the requested number of bytes: for example `FakeDigest().content_digest(b"x", "blake2b", size=48)` returns 64 hex characters, not the 96 hex characters a `blake2b` digest of `digest_size=48` must produce. chunk_findings.detail: `port` adds an arbitrary non-callable class attribute `__ddflow_port__ = True` to every Protocol it marks. The removed definitions in this same file show all moved ports (`Proc`, `Git`, `Fsio`, `Toml`, `Digest`, `HttpClient`) were `@runtime_checkable`; to keep being discovered they must now also be decorated with `@port`. The new line only passes the registered class to that factory: `entry.get("fake", lambda cls: cls())(F.FAKES[name])`. If a family entry says `"fake": lambda cls: GoodWidget()` while `F.FAKES["Widget"]` is `BrokenWidget`, the lambda ignores `cls`, returns a good stand-in, and the test passes even though `BrokenWidget` is never instantiated or exercised. The comment “always the REGISTERED fake” is therefore false; the produced instance should be asserted to be an instance of `F.FAKES[name]`.

chunk_findings.detail: The new test only checks that the returned string has length 1; it does not bound the amount of work done to produce it. If `FakeDigest.content_digest` were changed back to the previous pattern `while len(out) < max(want, self.WIDTH): ...` followed by slicing to `length`, the call `FakeDigest().of_obj({"a": 1}, size=10**9, length=1)` would still return a 1-character string and the test would pass, while the implementation would attempt to build a 2,000,000,000-character `out` string. Thus the test does not enforce the property stated in its docstring (“`length` bounds the work ... must not build a huge string”).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_digest.py:test_the_fake_builds_no_more_than_it_keeps

chunk_findings.detail: The new guard only checks `isinstance(made, F.FAKES[name])` after the family `fake` factory has already run, so it still does not force the conformance cases to exercise the registered fake class itself. If a family conformance entry provides `"fake": lambda cls: type("GoodWidget", (cls,), {"request": lambda self: "ok"})()` while `F.FAKES["Widget"]` is a broken `FakeWidget` whose `request` raises, the returned object is still an instance of `FakeWidget`, the assertion passes, and `entry["cases"]` runs against the subclass override rather than the registered fake. The assertion also reads `F.FAKES[name]` after the factory call, so a factory that mutates `F.FAKES[name]` can make the check pass against the mutated class. This contradicts the stated contract “always the REGISTERED fake”; a stronger check would snapshot `registered = F.FAKES[name]` before calling the factory and assert `type(made) is registered`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ports_contract.py:305 (`test_adapter_and_fake_pass_the_same_cases`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new guard only asserts `isinstance(made, F.FAKES[name])`, which accepts a subclass instance, not the registered class itself. A family can therefore keep a broken registered fake while its `CONFORMANCE` entry returns a subclass that overrides the broken behavior: for example, `F.FAKES["Widget"] = BrokenWidget` with methods that raise, and `CONFORMANCE["Widget"]["fake"] = lambda cls: GoodWidget` where `GoodWidget(BrokenWidget)` implements the methods. `isinstance(made, BrokenWidget)` is `True`, so the conformance cases run against `GoodWidget` and pass, while `BrokenWidget`—the class actually shipped in the registry—is never instantiated or exercised. Since the comment says “always the REGISTERED fake”, the assertion should require `type(made) is F.FAKES[name]` (or otherwise exercise that exact class), not merely an instance of it.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ports_contract.py:305

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeDigest` treats `size` only as a post-hoc truncation of a fixed CRC chain and caps that chain at `WIDTH = 64` hex characters. As a result, a requested `size` larger than 32 bytes is silently shortened: `FakeDigest().of_obj({}, size=64)` returns a 64-character hex string instead of the 128 characters implied by a 64-byte digest (and `content_digest(..., size=33)` returns 64 characters instead of 66). Worse, because `size` does not change the underlying chain, different `size` inputs can collapse to the same output when `length` is fixed: `FakeDigest().of_obj({}, size=12, length=24)` and `FakeDigest().of_obj({}, size=13, length=24)` both return the same first 24 hex characters, violating the fake’s stated “different inputs differ” property and any conformance case that treats `size` as a distinct digest-size input.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/digest.py:36

chunk_findings.detail: These methods are documented as context managers (“released on exit”, “removed on exit”) but are annotated as returning plain `Iterator` objects. A fake or adapter that satisfies the annotation by returning a generator, e.g. `def file_lock(self, path, *, timeout=None): yield`, is not a context manager, so the documented usage `with fsio.file_lock(path): ...` raises `AttributeError`/`TypeError` because the generator lacks `__enter__`/`__exit__`. Conversely, an implementation that correctly uses `@contextmanager` returns a `ContextManager`, not an `Iterator`, so it violates the protocol’s return annotation under structural type checking. The contract should require a context-manager type such as `ContextManager[Any]` and `ContextManager[Path]`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fsio.py: `Fsio.file_lock`, `Fsio.temp_text`

chunk_findings.detail: `port` is annotated as `(cls: Any) -> Any`, so using it as a class decorator erases the protocol type for static checkers. For example, after `@port class HttpClient(Protocol): ...`, an annotation such as `def send(client: HttpClient): ...` is typed `Any` by mypy, so passing an object without `request` is not reported. This defeats the stated purpose of ports being structural `Protocol` types and changes the static behaviour from the old `ports.py`, where `HttpClient` was a `Protocol`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/ports.py:port

chunk_findings.detail: `discover` keys the result by `cls.__name__` and silently overwrites duplicates. If `ddflow/adapters/alpha.py` and `ddflow/adapters/beta.py` both define `@port class Cache(Protocol): ...`, `discover(ddflow.adapters)` returns only the `Cache` from the later module (`beta`), not the one from `alpha`. The generic conformance test then sees only one `Cache` port, so a missing fake or missing baseline line for `alpha.Cache` would not fail the test. Duplicate port names should either be namespaced by module or rejected loudly, not dropped silently.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/ports.py:discover

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion intended to pin deterministic sorted-module discovery is self-referential: the expected list is built by iterating `found` itself, so it only checks that discovery order agrees with `P.module_names(A)`, not that `P.module_names(A)` is sorted. If the filesystem/environment causes `P.module_names(A)` to return `['zoo', 'alpha']` and `P.discover(A)` iterates that same order, `found` is `['ZooPort', 'AlphaPort']` and the RHS is also `['ZooPort', 'AlphaPort']`, so the test passes even though ports are not in sorted module order, contrary to the stated “sorted module names, no hash order” requirement.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ports_contract.py:test_the_ports_are_found_by_scanning_not_listed

chunk_findings.detail: The refactor no longer checks that `ddflow/adapters/ports.py` itself is declaration-only. `test_a_port_is_a_declaration_only` parses each discovered port module but filters the AST to classes with a `@port` decorator, and the only replacement for the old module-wide `test_ports_are_declarations_only` is `test_the_ports_base_imports_the_standard_library_alone`, which inspects imports. Therefore, if `ddflow/adapters/ports.py` is edited to add any executable non-`@port` code, e.g. `class Helper: print("imported")`, both new tests pass while the shared ports base now runs code at import time. The old test would have failed, so the change no longer enforces the stated invariant that `ports.py` is a pure base.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ports_contract.py:test_a_port_is_a_declaration_only

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `assert list(found) == expect and sorted(F.FAKES) == sorted(found)` only compares the *keys* of the global fake registry with the keys returned by `F.collect(F)`. It never checks that the values in `F.FAKES` are the fake classes discovered by `F.collect(F)`, nor that `F.FAKES` itself is in sorted module order. For example, if a previous test or a bad registration leaves `F.FAKES['Digest'] = object()` while `F.collect(F)` returns `{'Digest': FakeDigest}` and the expected sorted module grouping, both `list(found) == expect` and `sorted(F.FAKES) == sorted(found)` are true, so this test passes even though the actual registry used by `test_adapter_and_fake_pass_the_same_cases` contains the wrong fake. The test should compare values/identity (or compare `F.FAKES` directly to the discovered registry) rather than only sorted key sets.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ports_contract.py:test_fakes_register_in_sorted_module_order

chunk_findings.detail: The old module exposed `FakeDigest` as a top-level class and `FakeHttpClient` via `from .http import FakeHttpClient`, so `from ddflow.adapters.fakes import FakeDigest` or `from ddflow.adapters.fakes import FakeHttpClient` worked. The new code only runs `collect(...)`, and `importlib.import_module` of each submodule sets the submodule attributes `fakes.digest` and `fakes.http`, not the contained class attributes. Thus `ddflow.adapters.fakes.FakeDigest` now raises `AttributeError` and the old direct imports raise `ImportError`. This is a behavior change for shipped fakes and violates the no-behaviour-change requirement [D-adapters-answers].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/__init__.py:package namespace

chunk_findings.detail: The per-family docs for forge, fsio, git, proc and tomlcfg still say the default adapter is `ddflow.infra.<family>` (“Default adapter: `ddflow.infra.forge` today”). Under this change, `ddflow/adapters/<family>.py` is the family module that owns the port, default adapter and registry entry, so these docs point readers to the old pre-change location. A reader following `docs/ddflow/adapters/forge.md` is told to use `ddflow.infra.forge` rather than the new canonical `ddflow.adapters.forge` (same issue in `fsio.md:7`, `git.md:7`, `proc.md:7`, `tomlcfg.md:7`).
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/adapters/forge.md:7

chunk_findings.detail: The `HttpClient` conformance entry sets `"real": ScriptedUrllib`. But `ScriptedUrllib` is the scripted replacement for urllib calls used by the default adapter to avoid the network, not an implementation of the `HttpClient` port. The port interface is exercised by `http_conformance` as a `request` API, while `ScriptedUrllib` provides the transport/urllib side. When `pytest tests/test_ports_contract.py` runs the discovered http family via this `CONFORMANCE`, it will call `http_conformance` against `ScriptedUrllib` instead of the real `HttpClient` wired to `ScriptedUrllib`, and the cases will fail with an `AttributeError`/`TypeError` because the object does not implement the adapter's `request` method.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_http.py:CONFORMANCE

chunk_findings.detail: The guard subtracts the entire `LEGACY` set for every path ending `.md`, which includes `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`. Because `LEGACY` contains `Forge`, `Fsio`, `Proc`, `Toml`, and `Git`, a `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` that still has a per-family section such as “Forge” will pass the assertion, even though `[r-small-files]`/the intent says ARCHITECTURE.md must keep only the pattern and a link while per-family docs live in `docs/ddflow/adapters/<family>.md`. The exemption should only apply to `tests/test_ports_contract.py` and, if truly unavoidable, to the plain English word “Git” in ARCHITECTURE.md.

chunk_findings.detail: The `expr.id.isupper()` branch makes any all-caps `ast.Name` count as a literal. `_literal` is used by `_opaque`/`_class_code` to detect runtime code in a `@port` class, so this lets executable name references pass. For example, in `ddflow/adapters/http.py` define `TIMEOUT = 5` and then in the `@port` class use `def request(self, timeout: int = TIMEOUT) -> None: ...`; the default is evaluated at class-definition time, but `_literal(ast.Name("TIMEOUT"))` now returns `True`, so `_class_code` sees no statement and the test passes. Previously only `None`, `True`, and `False` names were allowed. The test's own wording says `frozenset(...)` is code “however cheap”, and a `LOAD_NAME` for `TIMEOUT` is runtime code too; this false negative weakens the declaration-only invariant the test is meant to enforce.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ports_contract.py:83 `_literal`

chunk_findings.detail: `expect` is derived from `found.items()`, so any fakes that discovery failed to register are omitted from both sides of the assertion. Given an environment where `F.collect` returns `{}` (e.g. the fake submodules are not imported, or the `fake` decorator no longer registers them), `expect` is also `[]`, so `list(found) == expect` is true and the test passes. The removed previous assertion compared `F.FAKES` against the explicit, non-empty `CASES`; with the new loops over `F.FAKES` also iterating zero entries when it is empty, broken fake discovery can leave all fake conformance checks silently unrun.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ports_contract.py:test_fakes_register_in_sorted_module_order

chunk_findings.detail: The new `size` fix ignores `length` when choosing how much of the CRC chain to generate. `want` is derived from `size * 2`, but the loop runs until `max(want, self.WIDTH)` even if the caller immediately truncates the result to a small `length`. For example, `FakeDigest().of_obj({"a": 1}, size=10**8, length=1)` should return one character quickly, but this code loops about 25 million times and builds a roughly 200 MB string before finally returning `out[:1]`. This is a new resource-exhaustion path introduced by the size fix; the loop only needs to generate up to `min(length, want)` when `length` is provided (or `want` when it is not).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/digest.py:35

chunk_findings.detail: The test’s name promises sorted-module registration, but the new assertions still do not pin sortedness of the module scan or of the global `FAKES` registry. `expect` is built by iterating `mods`, so if `P.module_names(F, frozenset())` returns `['zoo', 'alpha']` and `F.collect(F)`/`F.FAKES` are populated in that same order, then `list(found) == expect`, `all(F.FAKES[n] is c ...)`, `sorted(F.FAKES) == sorted(found)`, the module-set check, and the package-attribute check all pass even though the registry is not in sorted module order. Likewise, if `found` is sorted but `F.FAKES` insertion order is reversed, `sorted(F.FAKES) == sorted(found)` still passes because it compares only key sets. Thus an unsorted or nondeterministic fake registry can satisfy the test, contrary to the intended sorted-module discovery guarantee.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ports_contract.py:test_fakes_register_in_sorted_module_order

chunk_findings.detail: The new duplicate guard keys on `cls.__name__` but ignores the iteration variable `name`, so an alias to a decorated port class in the same module is misread as a second port. For example, if `ddflow/adapters/http.py` has `@port class HttpClient(Protocol): ...` followed by `PortAlias = HttpClient`, then `vars(module).items()` yields both names for the same class. Both entries pass `isinstance(cls, type) and cls.__dict__.get(MARK) and cls.__module__ == module.__name__`, and the alias then trips `if cls.__name__ in found`, raising `ValueError` even though there is only one port.

chunk_findings.detail: The same false-positive now exists for fakes. In `fakes/digest.py`, define `@fake class FakeDigest: ...` and `DigestAlias = FakeDigest`. Because the alias points to the same class, it still satisfies `cls.__dict__.get(MARK)` and `cls.__module__ == module.__name__`, so the second iteration sees `port` already in `found` and raises `ValueError('two fakes for Digest: ddflow.adapters.fakes.digest and ddflow.adapters.fakes.digest')`. There is still only one fake.

chunk_findings.detail: The dynamic alias restores runtime imports like `from ddflow.adapters.fakes import FakeDigest`, but static checkers do not treat `globals()[name] = ...` as a module attribute. A source file containing that import is then reported by mypy/pyright as having no attribute `FakeDigest`, whereas the previous explicit `from .digest import FakeDigest` was statically visible. The fix should expose the fake names statically, e.g. with a real declaration or a typed `__getattr__`.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `assert mods == sorted(mods)` only pins the module scan order; the test still derives `expect` from `found.items()`. If discovery/registration regress to producing no fakes — for example, the `fake` decorator stops registering classes, or `F.collect` fails to import the fake submodules so both `F.collect(F)` and `F.FAKES` are empty — then `mods` can still be sorted/non-empty, `expect` is empty, `list(found) == expect` is true, `all(...)` over an empty `found` is true, and `sorted(F.FAKES) == sorted(found)` is true. Thus the test can pass even though no fake was discovered or registered, so the previous confirmed gap (non-empty discovery / every fake module contributes a fake) is not answered by this diff.

chunk_findings.detail: The new test imports a temporary fake package through `F.collect(importlib.import_module("adp_fixture_alias.fakes"))`, which registers the temporary `FakeWidget` in the real global `ddflow.adapters.fakes.FAKES` registry (the same global state later checked by `test_ports_contract.py`). The `finally` block only deletes `sys.modules` entries and never removes that registry entry. In the default full-suite order `test_adapter_modularity.py` runs before `test_ports_contract.py`, so `test_fakes_register_in_sorted_module_order` subsequently calls `F.collect(ddflow.adapters.fakes)`; its `found` does not include the temporary `"Widget"`, and the existing assertion `assert sorted(F.FAKES) == sorted(found)` fails because `F.FAKES` still contains the leftover `"Widget"` key. The test must clean up its fake-registry side effect.

If `size` is the digest size in bytes, as `of_obj`’s default `size=12` (24 hex chars) implies, then `FakeDigest().content_digest(b"x", algo="blake2b", size=64)` returns a 64-character hex string instead of the 128 characters requested by `size * 2`; the same happens for `of_obj({}, size=64)`. chunk_findings.detail: `Fsio.file_lock` (and `temp_text` at line 35) are documented as context-manager contracts (“released on exit”, “removed on exit”), but their return annotations are `Iterator[...]`. A caller using the documented pattern `with fsio.file_lock(path):` is using a value typed as `Iterator[Any]`, which is not a context manager and has no `__enter__`/`__exit__`; conversely, an implementation that literally returns an `Iterator` is a plain generator, so entering it with `with` raises `AttributeError`. A typical correct implementation using `contextlib.contextmanager` returns `ContextManager[...]`, which does not satisfy the declared `Iterator[...]` contract.

chunk_findings.detail: `port` marks a Protocol by setting a non-callable class attribute `__ddflow_port__ = True`. The old ports were `@runtime_checkable`, and any new family module that keeps that decorator in order to preserve structural checks will now have a runtime-checkable Protocol with a non-method member. For example, after `@port @runtime_checkable class HttpClient(Protocol): def request(...): ...`, a call such as `issubclass(FakeHttpClient, HttpClient)` raises `TypeError: Protocols with non-method members don't support issubclass()` even when the fake implements `request`; before this marker existed, that check could return True. This is a behaviour change and breaks conformance/caller structural checks that rely on runtime protocols [D-adapters-answers]. The marker should be kept outside the Protocol class (for example, in a global set or external registry) rather than as a class attribute.

chunk_findings.detail: The digest page states that the default adapter is `ddflow.core.digest` “today”, while `docs/ddflow/adapters/README.md` states that the default adapter is the ONE implementation in the family module `ddflow/adapters/<family>.py` and that `adapters` is the bottom layer importing no other ddflow layer. These statements cannot both be true for the digest family: if the default adapter remains in `ddflow.core.digest`, then either the family module does not contain its default adapter (contradicting the documented pattern and the manifest’s new `ddflow/adapters/digest.py`, which already adds `content_digest`, `canonical`, and `of_obj`), or `ddflow/adapters/digest.py` must import `ddflow.core.digest` to expose it, violating the bottom-layer rule. A developer following `digest.md` would be sent to the wrong module for the default adapter.

A new port `Foo` with `ddflow/adapters/foo.py`, `docs/ddflow/adapters/foo.md`, and `tests/ports_without_fake/Foo.txt`, but no fake and no `tests/test_adapter_foo.py`, passes this test because `have_fake` is false and the test-file assertion is skipped. chunk_findings.detail: The new `_literal` shortcut treats every all-caps `ast.Name` as harmless. That helper is used by the declaration-only check, whose docstring explicitly says nothing may run “in a body, a decorator or a base.” Given a port module with `ALL_CAPS = some_decorator` and a class written as `@port` / `@ALL_CAPS` / `class P(Protocol): ...`, the decorator expression is an all-caps `Name`, so `_literal` returns `True` and the test accepts the class even though class creation calls `ALL_CAPS` and can run arbitrary code. The same shortcut also lets a method body consisting of a bare all-caps name pass, which is neither a docstring nor `...` and is not a literal.

chunk_findings.detail: The new file-based baseline is only checked one way: every port without a fake must have a baseline file, and baseline files may not name a port that already has a fake. It never checks that a baseline file names a declared port at all. If the `Git` port is removed (or `discover()` fails to find it) but `tests/ports_without_fake/Git.txt` is left behind, `_without_fake()` returns `{"Git"}`, `Git` is in `_CEILING`, `missing` does not contain it, and `baseline & have` is empty, so the test passes even though the baseline file is no longer for a missing port. If a `Git` port is later added without a fake, the stale baseline file excuses it, violating the stated invariant that a new port cannot be excused.

chunk_findings.detail: The conformance test is supposed to run the cases against the fake registered in `F.FAKES`, but it constructs the fake as `entry.get("fake", F.FAKES[name])()`. If a family module’s `CONFORMANCE[name]` dictionary contains a `fake` key, the registered fake is never instantiated or exercised. For example, if `F.FAKES["Widget"]` is a broken `BrokenWidget` while `tests/test_adapter_widget.CONFORMANCE["Widget"]["fake"]` points to a working `GoodWidget`, the parametrized test passes even though the actual discovered fake is broken. The documented `CONFORMANCE` contract in the same file only requires `real` and `cases`, so allowing `fake` to override the registry defeats the purpose of the auto-discovered fake contract.

chunk_findings.detail: The digest family module defines only the `Digest` Protocol port. It does not define or re-export the concrete default digest adapter, and it does not import `hashlib`, even though the module docstring says `hashlib` is imported here and the change intent says existing digest adapters are moved into their family module. The new conformance test `tests/test_adapter_digest.py::test_the_default_adapter_passes_the_digest_cases` therefore has no real adapter to import from the new canonical home, so an import such as `from ddflow.adapters.digest import <default digest adapter>` raises `ImportError` and the default-adapter conformance case fails. This is a missing implementation, not a layout-only change.

chunk_findings.detail: `FakeDigest.content_digest` fills `out` only to `self.WIDTH` (64 hex characters) before slicing it by `size * 2`. For `size` values above 32, the result is silently shorter than the requested number of bytes: for example `FakeDigest().content_digest(b"x", "blake2b", size=48)` returns 64 hex characters, not the 96 hex characters a `blake2b` digest of `digest_size=48` must produce. Since the fake is meant to pass the same conformance cases as the default `Digest` adapter, this makes the fake diverge for supported `blake2b` sizes greater than 32.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/digest.py:38

chunk_findings.detail: `port` adds an arbitrary non-callable class attribute `__ddflow_port__ = True` to every Protocol it marks. The removed definitions in this same file show all moved ports (`Proc`, `Git`, `Fsio`, `Toml`, `Digest`, `HttpClient`) were `@runtime_checkable`; to keep being discovered they must now also be decorated with `@port`. But `typing.Protocol` treats any non-callable member (other than its whitelisted dunders) as a non-method member, and `runtime_checkable` Protocols with non-method members do not support `isinstance`. For example, if a moved port is `@port`-marked and still `@runtime_checkable`, then `isinstance(some_object, ThatPort)` raises `TypeError` instead of returning True/False, breaking the existing runtime port checks that the old file explicitly enabled.

chunk_findings.detail: The replacement text asserts every outside dependency has “one default adapter beside the port, a shipped fake, and one set of conformance cases that runs against both.” But this same change adds `tests/ports_without_fake/Forge.txt`, `Fsio.txt`, `Git.txt`, `Proc.txt`, and `Toml.txt`, recording that those ports have no shipped fake, so the generic conformance test cannot run their cases against a fake. The old text in this file correctly qualified this with the ratchet (“the list of ports still without one only shrinks”); the new version drops that qualification and documents a contract stronger than the implemented one. A contributor following this section will expect `FakeProc`, `FakeFsio`, etc. and fake conformance cases that do not exist.

chunk_findings.detail: The page says “Default adapter: `ddflow.core.digest` today (compat; the home moves in with ADP-migrate-homes).” This contradicts the change’s stated intent that the digest adapter is moved into `ddflow/adapters/digest.py` as part of this task, and contradicts the README pattern added in this same change: “The default adapter is the ONE implementation in that module.” A reader following the page will look in `ddflow.core.digest` for the default adapter and not find the new per-family module layout; if the default adapter truly remains in `ddflow.core.digest`, the new layout violates the documented and intended rule. Either way this line is stale for this change.

chunk_findings.detail: Each of these five new pages says both “Fake: none yet” and “Conformance cases: with the fake.” That is self-contradictory for the current state of this change: there are no `FakeForge`, `FakeFsio`, `FakeGit`, `FakeProc`, or `FakeToml` fakes, and no `tests/test_adapter_{forge,fsio,git,proc,tomlcfg}.py` files; these families are represented only by their `tests/ports_without_fake/*.txt` baseline lines. A reader following the docs will look for conformance cases for a fake that does not exist, so these pages misdescribe the layout the change actually creates.

chunk_findings.detail: The HttpClient conformance entry sets `"real": ScriptedUrllib`. `ScriptedUrllib` is the test file’s scripted stand-in for `urllib` (the transport open call), not the default `HttpClient` adapter. The generic contract test is designed around `real` being a per-family factory that returns the adapter after patchup, as shown by the Digest entry’s `_real(monkeypatch)`. For HttpClient it will therefore run `http_conformance(ScriptedUrllib(monkeypatch))` (or otherwise pass `ScriptedUrllib` where a client is expected), and `http_conformance` calls `.request("GET", ...)` on the result, as the existing line in this same file does (`c.request("GET", "http://a/connection", timeout=3)`). `ScriptedUrllib` has no `request` method, so the new generic contract test fails and the real HttpClient adapter is not exercised through the conformance path.

chunk_findings.detail: The `LEGACY` set is subtracted from `names` before looping over all four `FORMER_SHARED` files, even though the comment says legacy names may remain only in the shrink-only baseline of `tests/test_ports_contract.py`. This overbroad exclusion means a moved legacy family such as `Forge` (which now has `ddflow/adapters/forge.py` and `docs/ddflow/adapters/forge.md`) will be ignored if it still appears in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `ddflow/adapters/ports.py`, or `ddflow/adapters/fakes/__init__.py`. The test would pass even though `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` is required to keep only the pattern and a link, so the check fails to enforce the intended no-shared-file-edit guarantee for legacy ports.

chunk_findings.detail: The new parameterized test passes the `@port`-decorated class node to `_class_code`, whose documented check covers exactly “not in a body, a decorator or a base.” The marker decorator `@port` is itself an `ast.Name` in the class's `decorator_list`; `_literal(ast.Name(id='port'))` is still `False` because `'port'` is not `"None"`, `"True"`, `"False"`, and `'port'.isupper()` is `False`. That decorator is therefore emitted as runnable-code statements, and the `assert not statements` will fail for every valid checked-in port (e.g. `HttpClient` in `ddflow/adapters/http.py`). The test can never pass for a port selected by `_port_nodes`.

chunk_findings.detail: The new fake construction still allows a family `CONFORMANCE` entry to bypass the registered fake. The line passes `F.FAKES[name]` to `entry.get("fake", lambda cls: cls())`, but it never checks that the object returned to `entry["cases"]` is an instance of the registered fake. For example, if `F.FAKES["Widget"]` is a `BrokenWidget` class whose methods raise but which still satisfies the port so `test_a_registered_fake_satisfies_its_runtime_checkable_port` passes, and the family module sets `CONFORMANCE["Widget"]["fake"] = lambda cls: GoodWidget()`, then `test_adapter_and_fake_pass_the_same_cases` runs the conformance cases against `GoodWidget()` and passes without ever instantiating or exercising `BrokenWidget`. The previous fix changed the factory argument but did not enforce “always the REGISTERED fake”; it should at least assert that the constructed fake is an instance of `F.FAKES[name]` (or remove the family-supplied fake factory).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_ports_contract.py:test_adapter_and_fake_pass_the_same_cases

chunk_findings.detail: The README’s first bullet still says a port “lives in its family module `ddflow/adapters/<family>.py`, beside its default adapter”, while the bullet changed in this diff now says the default adapter is in that module only after ADP-migrate-homes and that until then the family page names where it is. The family pages in this same diff put Forge, Fsio, Git, Proc, and Tomlcfg default adapters in `ddflow.infra.*` today, so the first bullet is false for the current tree and the README points to two different canonical locations. ARCHITECTURE.md repeats the unqualified “one default adapter beside the port”, making the same contradiction.
